transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03 14:30 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Tom Baxter (CTO, Luminexa), Priya Singh (VP Product), Jordan Lee (ML Eng), Avery Cole (Platform)

Summary: quick discovery to map their rerank/search flow, infra, and constraints.

[00:00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm sophie from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with miguel our systems eng. you all good on audio/video?
[00:00:08] Tom: yep all good, thanks sophie.
[00:00:12] Priya: hi, thanks for doing this. want to start with a quick overview of what we're trying to solve.
[00:00:20] Sophie: sure, do you want to kick off with the use case?
[00:00:23] Priya: yeah, so at a high level, search and recommendations — we have a rerank step after initial retrieval. currently we use open search for text search and pinecone for vectors, but it's getting expensive and slower at scale. goal is to unify and improve relevance while controlling cost.
[00:00:42] Miguel: thanks. when you say "rerank" can you walk me through the pipeline? initial retrieval, then embedding similarity, then model-based rerank?
[00:00:50] Jordan: exactly. pipeline is: user query -> BM25 via OpenSearch to get 200 candidates -> embed candidates and query -> approximate nearest neighbor re-score (we call it vector filter) -> top 20 go to a cross-encoder (transformer) for final rerank.
[00:01:10] Miguel: and the cross-encoder runs centrally or as a batch?
[00:01:14] Jordan: synchronous, it's our latency-critical path, currently hosted on GPUs in our cloud account, 250 ms P95 right now but that's at low QPS.
[00:01:24] Sophie: got it. what's your traffic profile, avg qps vs peak?
[00:01:29] Tom: avg about 500 qps for search endpoints, peak up to 6k during campaigns. most queries are short, 1-2 sentence queries.
[00:01:39] Priya: business wants p95 end-to-end under 400 ms for search (rerank included), and costs need to be predictable — especially during peaks.
[00:01:48] Miguel: that helps. what dim are you using for embeddings and which model?
[00:01:53] Jordan: right now we use a 768 dim model (open embedding), but evals show 1536 gives better recall on long-tail. storage and vector size is a concern though.
[00:02:04] Sophie: are you open to quantized embeddings or do you need full float storage?
[00:02:09] Jordan: probably okay with 16-bit or quantized 8-bit if it doesn't hurt recall, we want to test.
[00:02:15] Miguel: on the vector DB side, you mentioned pinecone — what similarity index and topology are you running?
[00:02:21] Jordan: currently pinecone with HNSW, single region, they shard automatically. the issue is tail latency during big campaigns.
[00:02:30] Avery: and our infra team is worried about data residency — some customers require logs not leave region. private deployment might be needed for that subset.
[00:02:38] Sophie: understood. we support three modes: hosted API for fastest time-to-value, dedicated reserved capacity pools for predictable throughput, and private VPC/on-prem for strict residency. any initial bias toward one?
[00:02:49] Tom: open to hosted for a pilot, but production probably dedicated or private depending on security review.
[00:02:56] Priya: yes, pilot hosted to validate quality, then dedicated or VPC for production.
[00:03:02] Miguel: makes sense. quick question on hybrid search — do you run BM25 + ANN in one step or hybrid rerank after retrieval?
[00:03:10] Jordan: retrieval by BM25 then ANN re-score, hybrid is basically combining BM25 score + vector similarity before rerank. we tune weights.
[00:03:20] Miguel: for throughput sizing, is the cross-encoder the biggest cost/latency?
[00:03:24] Jordan: yes, cross-encoder is heavy; but vector lookup also becomes expensive at high qps if vector dim is 1536 and not quantized.
[00:03:32] Sophie: have you evaluated Redwood's batching and cache features? automatic prefix/KV cache can reduce repeated token cost for the cross-encoder and batching for throughput.
[00:03:40] Priya: we saw your docs but would like numbers — how much improvement typically?
[00:03:44] Miguel: anecdotal: batching + KV cache can cut per-token cost by 30-60% depending on reuse. for rerank the benefit depends on sequence length and locality. we'll run estimates for your profile.
[00:03:56] [00:04:00] Tom: on security, we need SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration and audit logs. any red flags?
[00:04:08] Sophie: we have SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS), and full audit logs in the console. we'll share the security packet.
[00:04:17] Priya: and encryption at rest for dedicated/private?
[00:04:19] Miguel: yes, dedicated uses customer-managed keys if desired, and private deploys keep data in your VPC.
[00:04:25] Jordan: what about dimensionality — if we move to 1536 but quantize to 8-bit, how does that affect latency on your end?
[00:04:33] Miguel: quantization helps memory & lookup; our runtime supports quantized kernels and can trade slight recall for big cost/latency wins. we should benchmark your vectors.
[00:04:41] [00:04:45] Tom: can you support hybrid indexes — like combining a small faiss HNSW for shortlists and bm25 for initial?
[00:04:52] Miguel: yes, our routing and caching can support hybrid flows; many customers run BM25 initial then ANN, or run parallel retrieval and merge.
[00:05:00] Priya: timeline — we want pilot in 4-6 weeks and production in 12-16 weeks if results look good. is that feasible?
[00:05:08] Sophie: that timeline is realistic: pilot hosted within a couple weeks, then can move to dedicated/private depending on security review.
[00:05:15] Jordan: what about cost predictability on dedicated? we need steady unit economics for budgeting.
[00:05:20] Sophie: dedicated gives reserved capacity and predictable throughput with SLA; we can model cost for your peak window and suggest autoscale/burst options.
[00:05:28] Avery: platform question — network egress and VPC peering, do you require whitelisting, or can we set up a private link?
[00:05:34] Miguel: for private deployments we do VPC peering and options for private link; for hosted we support IP allowlists and private networking via partners. we'll share the network diagram and requirements.
[00:05:45] [00:05:50] Priya: stakeholders — who should be included for the technical deep dive?
[00:05:53] Tom: infra (avery), ml (jordan), security (me plus ciso) — we'll coordinate calendar.
[00:05:59] Miguel: great, for the deep dive we'll bring our infra architect and demo throughput numbers; we'll also propose a benchmark run on your sample data.
[00:06:07] Priya: question on migration — we have lots of data in pinecone, would migration be heavy?
[00:06:12] Sophie: we have migration support and can help with connectors; often customers seed a pilot and then do a bulk import. we'll provide docs.
[00:06:20] Jordan: curious about multi-tenancy and tenant isolation on dedicated — if we host multiple apps, can we isolate?
[00:06:26] Miguel: dedicated pools are isolated per customer and you can partition further with namespaces; RBAC applies per namespace.
[00:06:33] [00:06:35] Tom: any customers in regulated sectors running private?
[00:06:38] Sophie: yes, finance and health customers run private VPCs or on-prem packages; we can share redacted case studies.
[00:06:44] Priya: can you run a small POC: 1) hosted pilot with our sample dataset, 2) benchmark for 1k qps 512 dim and 5k qps 768/1536 quantized?
[00:06:55] Miguel: yes we can template that. we'll need your sample dataset and expected query distribution.
[00:07:00] [00:07:05] -- conversation continues with a few clarifying points --
[00:07:15] Jordan: one more technical — do you support vector shards colocated by doc type to reduce cold misses?
[00:07:21] Miguel: sharding strategies are flexible; we can colocate and use routing policies.
[00:07:26] Sophie: recap — pilot hosted, run benchmark (1k/5k qps scenarios), security packet + network diagram shared, schedule infra deep dive.
[00:07:35] Priya: perfect, appreciate it.
[00:07:38] Tom: thanks everyone.
[00:07:41] Sophie: action items as discussed, we'll follow up via email with the packet and calendar invite.
[00:07:45] [00:47:00] End of call
